answer: The insurance pool is funded by a levy on every settled reward, and claims are paid from that levy, so the cost of a clone farm is spread across the whole population rather than concentrated on whoever happens to catch it. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. Each identity contributes a wharf, a proved cluster triggers a lantern, and the ledge decides who receives it: one payer cannot absorb the whole lantern without exposing the ledge that makes the claim credible. Funding the levy is not optional either: it is deducted at settlement.
